test_title: SSC Selection Post Matric Level Official Paper (Held on: 14 March 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A man sells an article at a certain price. If he sells it at 35% less of this selling price, then he has a loss of 22%. If he sells it at its original selling price, then his profit percentage is:
solution:
Given:

A man sells an article at a certain price. If he sells it at 35% less of this selling price, then he has a loss of 22%.

Concept used:

Profit% = {(Selling Price - Cost Price) over Cost Price} times 100\%

Selling Price = Cost Price - Cost Price × Loss%

Incremented/Reduced value = Initial value (1 ± change%)

Calculation:

Let the cost and selling prices of the article be R and Q.

According to the question,

R - R × 22% = Q - Q × 35%

⇒ R - 0.22R = Q - 0.35Q

⇒ 0.78R = 0.65Q

⇒ R/Q = 0.65/0.78

⇒ R/Q = 5/6

So, the cost and selling prices are 5P and 6P respectively. (Considering P as the common ratio)

Now, his profit percentage = {{6P - 5P} over 5P} times 100\%

⇒ {{1} over 5} times 100\% = 20%

∴ His profit percentage is 20%.
